subject: art-design
title: Critical Analysis Terms: Foundations
welcome_lead: Build the basic critical vocabulary you will use in every essay.
meta_desc: GCSE critical analysis foundations: composition, palette, medium, scale.
final_note: The right words let you say exactly what you see.

concepts.def: How elements are arranged in the picture.
Material used to make the work.
Range of colours used in a work.
Size of work in relation to viewer.
What the work depicts or refers.
Recognisable manner of an artist or movement.

walkthroughs.body_html: Composition is how the artist arranged the picture. Subject matter is what it shows. Talk about both: "the subject is a vase of sunflowers, composed with the focal point on the rule-of-thirds intersection top right."

Identifying the medium (e.g. acrylic on canvas, charcoal on cartridge) is the first concrete fact in any analysis. The palette — warm earths, complementary blues and oranges — tells you the artist's emotional choices.

Scale changes meaning: a small intimate piece pulls the viewer close, a wall-sized work surrounds them. Style identifies a manner — gestural, photo-realistic, geometric — and often links the artist to a movement.
